project_specification.project_name: nullius — Stage 2 BingX VST: scheduled rebalances, flatten, daily-loss halt, fill-cost reconciliation
project_specification.addition_summary: Extend the router workspace member (packages/router, import name router) so the Stage 1 VST mirror runs on its own, under its risk limits, on the dedicated sub-account nullius01. Stage 1 places a book on demand (python -m router.bingx_mirror --place), reads it back (--status) and cancels it (--cancel). Every path is verified live and pinned against the recorded VST responses under packages/router/tests/fixtures/bingx_vst/live/. Stage 2 closes the gaps between that manual command and an unattended bot with four pieces: - a flatten that cancels every open order and closes every position; - a daily-loss guard wired to risk feature 325, which flattens and halts at 3% of the book's equity; - a per-rebalance fill-cost reconciliation recorded through forward feature 340; - a one-shot scheduled rebalance driven by a systemd user timer every 4 hours, which stamps rebalance_ts with the slot start so a re-run within a slot is idempotent. The target book still comes from a book file (the synthetic book today). Each rebalance is persisted into the book member's RebalanceTargetWeightsStore when the file names its originating signals, so swapping in real promoted signals later changes only the input.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (members under packages/*, composed by src/app/module_loader.create_app) / SQLite stores addressed by DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: workspace suite tests/ (1573) and packages/router/tests (1099) passing on main. Measure the real numbers before relying on them.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, stdlib-first members (the router adds no third-party dependency), docstrings citing app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, refusals raised as typed errors whose message opens with a greppable code word and names the one repair, defined in the module that raises them and subclassing router.errors.RouterError (router.errors and router/__init__.py are not edited). Decimal arithmetic from the venue's strings. Cross-member imports (book, risk, forward) are deferred past module scope. Follow CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section: iterate on one test file, then run the member suite once at -n 4. Tests never reach the network: clients are injected doubles. Every BingX response a test feeds must be a recorded fixture from packages/router/tests/fixtures/bingx_vst/live/ or built from one; never invent a response shape (Stage 1 lost eleven bugs to a stand-in that copied the spec instead of BingX). Existing pieces to reuse, not reimplement: - router.bingx_client.BingXClient: positions, balance, open_orders, place_order, cancel_order, query_order, position_mode, depth, contracts and premium_index; - router.bingx_mirror: build_mirror_plan, mirror_place, rebalance_order_identities and live_positions; - router.bingx_orders: read_back_orders and cancel_rebalance_orders; - risk.daily_loss: halt_on_daily_loss(daily_loss=, daily_loss_limit=), require_within_daily_loss_limit and manual_reset; - forward.reconciliation.reconcile_fill_costs(book_id, rebalance_ts=, realized_cost_bps=, modeled_cost_bps=); - book's RebalanceTargetWeightsStore.record(book_id=, rebalance_ts=, target_weights=, originating_signals=). BingX facts, verified live (see live/capture.json): - positionAmt is unsigned, with the side in positionSide; - open orders are listed under data.orders with the id spelled clientOrderId; - a DELETE's signed parameters go in the query string; - a single order is nested under data.order, and a resting order's status is PENDING; - the account is one-way (dualSidePosition false).

category.name: BingX VST Stage 2
category.feature: System flattens the VST sub-account from `python -m router.bingx_flatten --confirm`: it cancels every open order on the account, then closes every position with one reduce-only MARKET order per symbol (side opposite to positionSide, quantity the unsigned positionAmt, positionSide BOTH, reduceOnly true). It prints one JSON line per cancelled order and per close, and returns exit 0 only when a final read shows no open orders and no positions. Without --confirm it prints what it would do and changes nothing. A close the venue refuses is printed with its code and message, and the run exits 1.

System guards each rebalance with a daily-loss check before anything is placed. The first check of each UTC day records the account's equity as that day's opening equity, in its own table in the DATABASE_URL store. Each check computes daily_loss as opening equity minus current equity. When daily_loss reaches 3% of the book's equity_usdt, it trips risk.daily_loss.halt_on_daily_loss, flattens through feature 1 and returns a daily_loss_halt refusal. While a halt stands, require_within_daily_loss_limit refuses every later check with orders_halted, places nothing, and keeps refusing until risk.daily_loss.manual_reset. A profit or a smaller loss passes.

System reconciles one finished rebalance's fill costs. It reads back the rebalance's orders with read_back_orders and takes each filled order's executedQty and avgPrice. The realized cost in basis points is the notional-weighted signed slippage of avgPrice against the order's reference price (adverse is positive), plus the fee rate the order paid. The fee is makerFeeRate for a PostOnly LIMIT and takerFeeRate for a MARKET order, from the contracts document. The modeled cost is that same fee rate alone. It records both through forward.reconciliation.reconcile_fill_costs(book_id, rebalance_ts=, realized_cost_bps=, modeled_cost_bps=), and returns the recorded reconciliation. A rebalance with no filled order records nothing and returns none. Reconciling the same rebalance twice returns the first record unchanged.

System runs one scheduled rebalance slot from `python -m router.bingx_rebalance --book BOOK` and prints one JSON summary line. The slot is the current UTC time floored to a 4-hour boundary, and rebalance_ts is the slot start, so a second run in the same slot prints prior for every order and places nothing new. In order, a slot: 1. runs feature 2's daily-loss guard; 2. cancels resting orders left by this book's earlier slots in the last 24 hours, using rebalance_order_identities per slot; 3. reconciles the previous slot through feature 3; 4. builds and places the plan through build_mirror_plan and mirror_place; 5. persists the rebalance into the book member's RebalanceTargetWeightsStore when the book names originating_signal_ids. It exits 0 when every order is placed or prior, 1 when any leg is refused, and 3 on a daily-loss refusal. It refuses to start without DATABASE_URL. deploy/systemd/ holds a user service that runs `./run.sh vst-rebalance --book packages/router/tests/fixtures/bingx_vst/synthetic_book.json` from the repository root as a oneshot, and a timer that fires it at 00:05, 04:05, 08:05, 12:05, 16:05 and 20:05 UTC, with Persistent=true and no overlapping runs.

project_specification.integration_points: Four new modules under packages/router/src/router/: bingx_flatten.py, bingx_risk.py, bingx_reconcile.py and bingx_rebalance.py. bingx_flatten and bingx_rebalance are runnable with python -m. Their tests sit in packages/router/tests/, and the systemd units sit in deploy/systemd/. Each file is committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves. run.sh already routes `./run.sh vst-rebalance` and `./run.sh vst-flatten` to the two entry points under op run with .env.vst.tpl (the VST key only) and DATABASE_URL defaulting to ~/.local/share/nullius/vst.db. The placement store, the daily-loss halt, the opening-equity table and the fill-cost reconciliation all live in that one store. Stage 1 modules are reused through their public functions. Their files, and router.errors and router/__init__.py, are not edited.
project_specification.constraints: - The only host reachable is open-api-vst.bingx.com, through BingXClient's host guard. There is no live-host path. - No test or task opens a network connection, reads 1Password or a credential, or edits .env.tpl, .env.vst.tpl, run.sh, claw-forge.yaml or claw-forge.local.yaml. - Every BingX response used in a test is a recorded fixture from packages/router/tests/fixtures/bingx_vst/live/ or derived from one. Those fixtures are never edited. - Nothing in this addition installs or enables the systemd units. Writing the files is the deliverable; enabling them is an operator step. - Flatten acts only through --confirm or through the daily-loss guard. Nothing else can close positions. - The Stage 1 modules (bingx_client, bingx_documents, sizing, bingx_client_order_id, bingx_order, bingx_dry_run, bingx_preflight, bingx_orders, bingx_mirror) keep their public behaviour and their tests stay green unchanged. - No change to packages/ingest, packages/book's, packages/risk's or packages/forward's source, src/app/module_loader.py, the root pyproject.toml, uv.lock, migrations/** or settings. - Do not edit docs/user-journeys/: verdicts there are set only by browser runs. - All existing workspace and member tests must stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1: flatten (feature 1) and fill-cost reconciliation (feature 3), independent, over injected client doubles built from the live fixtures.
Phase 2: the daily-loss guard (feature 2), over risk.daily_loss and feature 1's flatten.
Phase 3: the scheduled rebalance slot and the systemd units (feature 4), composing features 1–3 with Stage 1's planning and placement.
